summary: The submission benchmarks linear subspace intervention on Qwen2.5-14B, showing that a 7-dimensional subspace learned from 8 digits at block 10 successfully steers downstream addition and subtraction assertion outcomes across 511 evaluation pairs. The experimental design incorporates both norm-matched random controls and full activation transfers with exact environment documentation, though evaluation remains restricted to a single architecture and layer.
strengths: Rigorous experimental controls, pairing the learned subspace intervention against an equal-norm random orthogonal subspace (0/511 reversals) and full activation exchange positive control (511/511 reversals).
Precise reproducibility documentation specifying the exact Hugging Face snapshot commit hash (`97e1e76335b7017d8f67c08a19d103c0504298c9`), dependency versions, and Apple Silicon hardware.
Careful task isolation ensuring the candidate arithmetic outputs differ from source digits to confirm functional consequence rather than token copying.
weaknesses: Evaluated on only a single model checkpoint (Qwen2.5-14B) and a single intermediate layer (block 10), without layer-sweep sensitivity analysis.
Limited arithmetic scope restricted to single-step additions and subtractions with small constants.
Very compact writeup (under 500 words) that omits deeper qualitative error analysis on the single ineligible pair.
suggestions: Conduct a layer ablation across all 48 transformer blocks to determine where numerical value representations solidify and where steering begins to degrade.
Expand benchmark evaluation across model scales (e.g., Qwen2.5-7B, 32B, and 72B) and operations (e.g., multiplication, multi-digit arithmetic) to test generalizability.
